Definition: a Levite or descendant of Levi
BiblicalUsage: Levites are what Lêvîyîy means — descendants of Levi, set apart for the work of the tabernacle and the temple. In Numbers 3:12, "I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix among the children of Israel: therefore the Levites shall be mine"; and in Deuteronomy 18:1, "The priests the Levites". In 1 Chronicles 6:48, "Their brethren also the Levites [were] appointed unto all manner of service of the tabernacle of the house of God."; and in Ezra 2:40, "The Levites: the children of Jeshua and Kadmiel".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Levites are God's chosen servants — taken instead of the firstborn, set apart to bear the ark, and given the tithes for their work. I hold that their service is the pattern of mine: appointed by God, sustained by God's people, and offered back to God. My position is that I do not choose my service; the Lord takes me for it, as He took Levi.
